chunks: By the One who sent him

You will be severely subverted, bitterly shaken as in sieving and fully mixed as by spooning in a cooking pot, till your low persons become high and high ones become low, those who were behind would attain forward positions and those who were forward would become backward.

key_terms.سَوْطَ الْقِدْرِ: the stirring of the pot (metaphor for thorough mixing and turmoil)
key_terms.غَرْبَلَةً: sifting or sieving (metaphor for testing and separating)

ai.seo_question: What does the metaphor of 'sifting and stirring' mean in Nahj al-Balagha regarding social upheaval?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) delivers this prophecy to the people of Medina upon their allegiance, foretelling the chaotic social inversion and political turmoil that would follow his caliphate, particularly during the era of the Khulafa'. The metaphors of 'balbalah' (confusion/mixing) and 'gharbalah' (sieving/testing) highlight the purification of the faithful through the upheaval where the last shall be first and the first last, a theme deeply resonant with Shia eschatological expectations of justice prevailing after initial disorder.
